## Requirements: Persistent typed tmux Control Mode Client for Nession Agent

### Background and decision (2026-10-24)

**Owner decision:** Implement a first-class, long-lived **`TmuxClient`** that encapsulates the tmux Control Mode protocol, command/response dispatch, byte-exact event stream and connection lifecycle. Follow the strong Client/API boundary seen in [ArcavenAE/tmux-cmc](https://github.com/ArcavenAE/tmux-cmc), **without importing that implementation wholesale**.

Nession already has:
- `tmux/cmd.rs::TmuxCmd` for explicit private `-S <absolute path>` addressing and safe process spawning;
- `tmux/ops.rs::TmuxOps` as the *canonical reusable tmux operation grammar* (completed #991);
- `tmux/control.rs::ControlModeSession` using `tmux -C attach` over pipes, with a control-channel bootstrap/capture barrier;
- `tmux/session.rs::TmuxSession` for separate Control Mode and plain PTY attach backends;
- the Agent Session Terminal Stream Owner, epoch/seq/replay/ACK and P2P/Relay parity governed by [Terminal Consistency RFC v2](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/main/docs/design/terminal/ahp-inspired-terminal-consistency.md) (#1645).

These are **not** to be replaced with competing authorities. Currently `ControlModeSession::write_input` and `resize` primarily confirm command bytes reached the child stdin, not that the tmux command returned `%end` rather than `%error`. Also the Control Mode ingress exposes output and resize through separate receiver/consumer paths; a strict source-order guarantee through Agent stream sequencing must be characterized and proved rather than assumed.

The upstream [tmux Control Mode spec](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/wiki/Control-Mode) and tmux 3.6b [client.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/3.6b/client.c) / [control.c](https://github.com/tmux/tmux/blob/3.6b/control.c) show that `-C` and `-CC` share the same Control Mode message grammar. The distinction is transport/TTY handling: `-C` permits separate stdin/stdout pipes; `-CC` configures termios, uses its stdin TTY as the bidirectional protocol FD and adds startup DCS / exit ST markers. **`-CC` cannot be substituted into the existing pipe-spawn without a PTY transport.**

### Ownership and scope

```text
Nession Agent Session / TerminalStreamOwner
    |  typed tmux operations and ordered source events
    v
TmuxClient (session-owned, not WebSocket-owned)
    +-- typed command API + response completion/error
    +-- one ordered, bounded event ingress
    +-- lifecycle/handshake/fault notification
    +-- byte-framed Control Mode parser (reuse #2300 work)
    +-- Transport: Pipe (-C) | PTY (-CC)
    |
    +-- existing TmuxCmd for explicit -S, subprocess safety
    +-- existing TmuxOps as the single command-grammar owner
    v
tmux server / windows / panes / applications
```

**The Client owns:** one long-lived control attachment, transport IO and framing, typed tmux ids/command responses, notification subscription, source event order, command completion and shutdown/error behavior. It exposes a `TmuxEvent` carrying **raw `Vec<u8>`** for pane output, authoritative layout/size changes, relevant pane/session/mode lifecycle signals, and terminal/source loss. No `String` round-trip for arbitrary pane bytes.

**Nession still owns:** Session lifecycle and one-controller ControlLease, stream `epoch/seq`, checkpoint/replay, subscriber credit/ACK, P2P vs Relay, xterm applied cursor and TUI fidelity. The Client must not become a second stream owner or a VT emulator.

**Explicit implementation decision:** Support and **actually test** both `-C + Pipe` and `-CC + PTY` inside one transport-independent Client API. Keep `-C + Pipe` as the initial production default until parity and operational evidence justify changing it; `-CC` is an implementation deliverable, not merely a future note. A controlled selection mechanism is sufficient; no end-user settings/UI required.

**Session ownership:** a control attachment belongs to the Agent's active session runtime, not the WebSocket that first attached. Disconnecting/replacing a P2P/Relay subscriber must not itself kill a still-owned tmux pane/session. Reconnect/attach and Agent shutdown must deterministically retire/replace the correct connection generation. Avoid creating an unbounded global pool or a potentially destructive `new-session -A -D` housekeeping session.

### Implementation boundaries

1. **Transport and handshake:** expose a testable IO/Transport seam; retain `TmuxCmd`-owned `-S` socket and inherited `TMUX` / `TMUX_TMPDIR` isolation. For `-CC`, create a valid PTY pair, set appropriate raw/termios behavior, explicitly handle DCS `ESC P 1000 p`, ST `ESC \\`, `%exit`, CRLF transformation and initial handshake; surface invalid PTY/termios and early child death. Do not blindly paste the pipe-based `-C` process setup.
2. **Byte-exact parser:** consume the bounded byte framing/error semantics from #2300 / PR #2301 **after its supported revision lands**; do not create a second decoder. Recognize `%begin/%end/%error` response blocks, `%output` (and any enabled `%extended-output`), known notifications and unknown forward-compatible notifications without misclassifying response data.
3. **Request/response dispatch:** one ordered command writer and bounded pending command queue; associate replies with the *actual tmux response order/serial semantics*, not fabricated client serial equality. Registration/write must be ordered atomically. Timeout/cancellation and late replies must never deliver a stale result to the next waiter (preserve an ordered tombstone or retire/re-establish the connection); reject all pending commands on terminal source failure. Distinguish written/accepted command from successfully completed tmux command and observed state.
4. **Single ordered event ingress:** output, authoritative resize/layout and source lifecycle notifications must enter the Agent Stream Owner in original source order (no independent consuming tasks that can resequence stream mutations). Preserve pane identity/selection and typed session/window/pane IDs; unrecognized notifications must be forward-compatible without hiding known protocol faults.
5. **Capture and recovery:** preserve the proven same-control-channel bootstrap barrier (#2124) with no lost/duplicated effects across capture and live data. A transport/reader failure must invalidate the *matching* Client generation/source stream and fail closed; do not falsely claim full VT fidelity, stream continuity or applied ACK after a gap. Keep event queues and memory bounded; do not invent a second replay or opaque `tmux-cmc` flow-control protocol.
6. **Integrate incrementally:** adapt `ControlModeSession` and Agent consumers to `TmuxClient`, preserve plain `PtySession` as a distinct backend where still needed. Share one canonical tmux operation grammar: `TmuxOps` remains the operation owner, and control-channel encoding is its transport-specific adapter. Keep process-invocation `TmuxCmd` for bootstrap, cold session management and documented fallbacks.
7. **Real environment proof:** a deterministic fake Control Mode fixture for protocol edge cases; real private-socket tmux on Linux and macOS for pipe/PTy parity; test real attach/input/output/capture/resize and representative normal-screen/alt-screen TUI. Instrument exact producer/client byte/event ordering rather than inferring it from final screenshots.

### Suggested delivery slices (independent PRs; no large one-shot rewrite)

- **A — Prerequisite:** close/merge the scoped P0 byte-framing repair #2300 / PR #2301. Reuse those guards; don't rebundle.
- **B — Client core:** transport-independent `TmuxClient`, typed API/events, command matcher and deterministic fake-wire tests. Adapt `-C + Pipe` without changing Nession's external behavior.
- **C — Session/runtime migration:** move `ControlModeSession` and the ordered Agent event ingress onto the Client; preserve capture barrier, ownership and end-to-end stream invariants.
- **D — `-CC + PTY` implementation:** same public Client API with verified PTY termios/DCS/ST and macOS/Linux tests; keep `-C` default until explicit parity evidence.
- **E — Cleanup:** remove superseded parser/writer/command duplications only after all production call sites have migrated; document transport tradeoffs and fallback.

All runtime PRs follow the repository's **staging-first** workflow and use isolated worktrees. A new separate crate is **not** a prerequisite; start in `crates/nession-agent/src/tmux/client/` and extract only after the boundary is stable. Preserve the `tmux-socket-isolation` Gate.

### Out of scope

- Replacing `TmuxOps` semantic ownership (#991), rewriting plain PTY behavior without a proven reason, new Nession wire protocol units, Agent global durable logs, VT emulator/full-TUI checkpoint, Web design changes, or reimplementing #1645 Replay/ACK/credit.
- Solving #2283 browser-local xterm resize race or #2286 device ControlLease takeover inside this refactor; instead prove they are not regressed.
- Promoting `-CC` to default solely because another Rust library uses it. No unwarranted throughput/performance claims without benchmark evidence.

### Success Criteria

- [ ] SC-01 Nession Agent exposes a session-owned typed `TmuxClient` with connect, command, event subscription and explicit close/source-loss semantics; caller code need not parse Control Mode wire lines or own the child stdin.
- [x] SC-02 Both `-C + Pipe` and `-CC + PTY` successfully handshake, execute commands and deliver equivalent typed pane output/layout events on real isolated tmux; the `-CC` DCS/ST, termios and invalid-Pipe negative path are handled explicitly on supported macOS/Linux runners.
- [x] SC-03 Valid arbitrary pane bytes including non-UTF-8, octal control bytes, CR/LF, split/large frames and interleaved command output arrive byte-identically; malformed/oversized frames and unknown notifications have bounded, intentional outcomes, reusing the #2300 contract.
- [x] SC-04 Concurrent commands receive the correct matching tmux `%end/%error` result in wire order; timeout, cancellation, disconnect and late reply cannot misdeliver a response to a later caller, with deterministic red/green fault fixtures.
- [x] SC-05 From the single Client source, output and authoritative size/layout changes preserve source order through Agent epoch/seq; capture/live straddling and source failure do not lose/duplicate data or falsely declare a verified checkpoint/continuity.
- [ ] SC-06 Reattach, WebSocket/P2P/Relay replacement and PC↔mobile subscriber transitions do not leak/kill unrelated tmux sessions or leave stale Client generations writing; one stalled consumer cannot indefinitely block the Client or healthy peers.
- [ ] SC-07 Every tmux spawn/cleanup still uses Nession's explicit private `-S` socket, canonical operations and safe ownership; a failed `-CC` launch reports failure without touching any default tmux server or silently switching transport.
- [ ] SC-08 Normal shell, Vim/top-style full-screen TUI, resize, exit, capture bootstrap and relevant existing P2P/Relay regression fixtures remain functional using the migrated Client; the new implementation does not assert complete VT restoration from screen-only capture.

## Product alignment

- [x] Supports [VISION.md](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/main/VISION.md): persistent, seamless cross-device work without rebuilding context.
- [x] Obeys [PRINCIPLE.md](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/main/PRINCIPLE.md): infrastructure complexity stays inside Agent, no new permanent UI.
- [x] Checked [Terminal Consistency RFC v2](https://github.com/BestNathan/nession/blob/main/docs/design/terminal/ahp-inspired-terminal-consistency.md); preserves Agent stream/session owners.
- [x] Prototype decision: **Not needed** — internal protocol/runtime refactor; real tmux and deterministic Cases are the proof, not a UI mock.

### Related work and deduplication

- #991 **closed:** canonical `TmuxOps` command semantics; do not reopen or duplicate.
- #93 **closed:** earlier tmux manager/trait reorganization; different invariant.
- #2300 / PR #2301 **prerequisite:** byte-safe framing/source-loss handling.
- #2124 **closed:** verified control-channel epoch-start capture barrier; must remain intact.
- #1645 / RFC v2: terminal stream owner, replay, ACK, fidelity authority.
- #2283: browser resize/parser ordering, separate repair; #2286: active-client resize authority, separate policy.
- [tmux-cmc reference](https://github.com/ArcavenAE/tmux-cmc): borrow the client/request/event split while explicitly rejecting its UTF-8 `String` assumption, unbounded notification channels and simplistic response cancellation.

---
**Status:** Approved — owner explicitly requested implementation of the encapsulated Client; implementation and acceptance are pending.
